q-88273.name: Question 4
q-88273.worked_solution:
Given two $n\times n$ matrices $M$ and $N,$ we have

$$
det(MN)=det(M)\cdot det(N).
$$

In our case, this gives

$$
det(H)=det[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 6 \\ 3 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]\cdot det[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

We can compute the required determinants as follows:

- For the first determinant, we can compute it using a Laplace expansion across the $3$rd row.

- For the second determinant, we can compute it using a Laplace expansion down the $2$nd column.

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -6 \\ 3 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}|\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =4(-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}|\cdot 3(-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =4(2-(-6)\cdot 3(2-3) \\  & =32\cdot (-3) \\  & =-96.\end{aligned}
$$

Given an invertible $n\times n$ matrix $A,$ we have

$$
det({A}^{-1})=\frac{1}{det(A)}.
$$

First, we find $det(A):$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =det[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =12+3 \\  & =15\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A| & =|B|\cdot |C| \\  & =24\cdot \frac{1}{4} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that the $1$st row of our determinant is almost equal to the $3$rd row. So, we can rewrite the given determinant, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}160 & 184 & 76 \\ 3 & 4 & -8 \\ 160 & 184 & 78\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}160 & 184 & 76 \\ 3 & 4 & -8 \\ 160+0 & 184+0 & 76+2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Next, using the linearity property of determinants, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}160 & 184 & 76 \\ 3 & 4 & -8 \\ 160+0 & 184+0 & 76+2\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}160 & 184 & 76 \\ 3 & 4 & -8 \\ 160 & 184 & 76\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}160 & 184 & 76 \\ 3 & 4 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

The first determinant must be zero since it has two identical rows, while the second determinant can be expanded across the $3$rd row, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}160 & 184 & 76 \\ 3 & 4 & -8 \\ 160 & 184 & 76\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}160 & 184 & 76 \\ 3 & 4 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| & =0+2(-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}160 & 184 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (160\cdot 4-184\cdot 3) \\  & =2\cdot 88 \\  & =176\end{aligned}
$$
